resources.string: Identifiers separated by spaces. Prefix a token with ! to force an airway, or with = to force a waypoint. Coordinates work too: N48.82/E2.62 or N48,8200/E2,62000.
This route also carries a procedure or an approach, which the box above cannot show. Editing the text would drop it. The preview below is what will be sent.
The navigator should now report \"1 new imported flight plan available for preview\". Open Flight Plan → Catalog on the unit to preview and accept it.
Bluetooth permission is needed to reach the navigator.
The navigator will not talk to an unauthenticated client. Import the Connext credential once to continue.
Not certified avionics. Check the plan on the navigator before you fly it. Not affiliated with Garmin.
No paired devices. Pair the navigator in Android Settings first. It will show its own confirmation prompt on the panel.
No Connext service. Probably not a navigator.
Another app may be holding the link
Powered off or out of range. You can still try.
Pick the navigator you are sending to. The model sets how long identifiers and the route string may be, and it cannot be detected over the link.

Each model\'s limits come from reading its own flight plan parser. A model that has not been read is left out rather than given another\'s numbers. A wrong limit fails the upload instead of trimming a name.
The GTN Xi is missing for that reason. If you have one and would let it be tested, open an issue at %1$s

A navigator will not take a flight plan from an unauthenticated client, and there is no way for an independent app to be issued a credential of its own. SendFPL carries the one Garmin\'s apps use. Nothing is asked of you, and it goes nowhere but the navigator.
If Garmin changes it, uploads stop working until SendFPL is updated. Replace lets you supply your own in the meantime:
Stored encrypted, and kept out of backups. Forget clears it until the app next starts.
Sends flight plans from your phone to a panel navigator over Bluetooth.
SendFPL is not certified avionics. The navigator holds an imported plan for preview. Check every waypoint there before you accept it. The pilot in command is responsible for the plan flown.

SendFPL is an independent project by %1$s, not affiliated with or endorsed by Garmin Ltd. Garmin, Connext, GTN, GNX and GNC are their trademarks, used here only to name the equipment this app talks to.
SendFPL has no network permission, so nothing leaves your phone. It keeps the credential, and which navigators you have uploaded to and when. Both stay on the device, and uninstalling removes them.
Free and open source under the MIT licence, at %1$s.
SendFPL carries the credential it authenticates with. If Garmin ever changes it, you can supply your own here without waiting for an update.
Bugs, feature requests, and navigators that are missing go to the issue tracker.
that file is bigger than %1$s, which is far more than this needs. It is probably not the file you meant to pick
A route needs at least a departure and an arrival, for example \"KSFO KLAS\".

\"%1$s\" is ambiguous: a latitude holds %2$d digits of degrees, so the decimal point could belong to the degrees or to the minutes. Write decimal degrees, %3$d digits for whole minutes, or %4$d digits for tenths of a minute.

\"%1$s\" is ambiguous: a longitude holds %2$d digits of degrees, so the decimal point could belong to the degrees or to the minutes. Write decimal degrees, %3$d digits for whole minutes, or %4$d digits for tenths of a minute.
Cannot read the latitude \"%1$s\". Write decimal degrees, %3$d digits for whole minutes, or %4$d digits for tenths of a minute.
Cannot read the longitude \"%1$s\". Write decimal degrees, %3$d digits for whole minutes, or %4$d digits for tenths of a minute.
\"%1$s\" has a hemisphere letter at both ends of one coordinate.
\"%1$s\" gives latitude %2$s, which is outside 90 degrees north to 90 degrees south.
\"%1$s\" gives longitude %2$s, which is outside 180 degrees east to 180 degrees west.
The waypoint name \"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and this navigator reads %3$d. A longer name loses the point its position.
The waypoint name \"%1$s\" has to be letters and digits only.
The departure aerodrome \"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and the %3$s reads %4$d.
The arrival aerodrome \"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and the %3$s reads %4$d.
The waypoint \"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and the %3$s reads %4$d. Shortening it would name a different place, so the route is not sent.
The airway \"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and the %3$s reads %4$d.
The procedure \"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and the %3$s reads %4$d.
The transition \"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and the %3$s reads %4$d.
\"%1$s\" is %2$d characters and this navigator reads %3$d. The file gave it as an identifier, so shortening it would name a different waypoint.
This route is %1$d bytes and the %3$s rejects anything over %2$d. Send it in two legs.
This is not a route file this reads. It takes a Garmin .fpl or .gfp, a GPX, a KML, a SkyDemon .flightplan, or a flight simulator .pln.
This file is not readable. A route has to be the file the planner exported, not a screenshot of it or a copy pasted into a document.
This is a zip. A KMZ has to be unzipped to the KML inside it first.
This is a SkyDemon waypoint library, not a route: a set of places with no order to fly them in. Open a route instead, or plan one through these points and export that.
This file holds fewer than two points, so there is no route in it.
Every point in this route is at the same place, so there is nothing to fly.
This file gives a position at %1$s, %2$s, which is not on the earth.
This file gives a position that is not a number.
